subject: Re: Stitching AWS/GCP marketplace lines for Nimbus merchant invoice
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Nimbus Analytics Billing <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 Nov 2029 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Stitching AWS/GCP marketplace lines for Nimbus merchant invoice

Hi Ana,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. We're reviewing the November marketplace invoices and we see a ~35% delta between the usage reported on the Nimbus ledger and the AWS/GCP marketplace payout lines for the same merchant ID (merchant:nimbus-534).

Quick ask to move this to resolution: could you send the following artifacts by EOD Monday so we can stitch the records?
- CSV export of Nimbus's internal usage for merchant:nimbus-534 covering 2029-11-01 to 2029-11-30 (UTC timestamps preferred)
- Any mapping table you use to attribute internal project IDs to marketplace product SKUs
- If you already filed evidence with AWS or GCP, please forward those support case IDs

I'll attach the partial manifests we have on our side so we can align: redwood_audit_manifest_20291203.xlsx (contains our merchant mapping and the lines we can't reconcile).

We suspect most of the delta is coming from two sources: (1) usage-window cutoffs between UTC and local processing that split tokens into adjacent billing windows, and (2) duplicated metering events from the AWS Marketplace event retries we saw on 11/12–11/14. If you can include any logs that capture sample request IDs around that period, that will speed things up.

Proposed next step after we receive artifacts: our billing team (cc'd) will stitch the CSVs and surface a short reconciliation summary with proposed credit adjustments or reallocation of lines to the right invoice. If needed, we'll open joint support cases with AWS/GCP.

Appreciate it — small turnaround here helps keep month-end collections on track.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Finance Partnerships — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood_audit_manifest_20291203.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ana Cortez <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Platform Eng <platform@nim-biz.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Nov 2029 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stitching AWS/GCP marketplace lines for Nimbus merchant invoice

Hi Marcus,

Thanks — received. I'm attaching our internal export (nimbus_usage_2029-11.csv) and a small lookup we use to map our internal project codes to marketplace SKUs.

Quick context: we had a customer migration mid-month where several projects were split across two internal IDs; that may account for some of the line-level mismatch. We also logged multiple 5xx retries from our side on 11/13 which generated duplicate metering submissions — we've flagged those in the CSV (column: suspect_duplicate = TRUE).

We've not yet opened a cloud marketplace support case; I'm happy to do that but would prefer Redwood's confirmation of the suspect events before we escalate. If you need us to open with AWS/GCP, tell me the text to include and we'll file it (we include request IDs and sample payloads in the ticket).

Also attaching a small sample of the event IDs we think are duplicates.

Best,
Ana Cortez
Head of Finance Ops — Nimbus Analytics
billing@nimbus-analytics.com
+1 (206) 555-4477

Attachments: nimbus_usage_2029-11.csv (csv), nimbus_project_sku_map_2029-11.csv (csv), sample_event_ids_11-13.txt (txt)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Nimbus Analytics <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Dec 2029 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stitching AWS/GCP marketplace lines for Nimbus merchant invoice

Ana — great, got everything. Quick internal notes below and proposed joint timeline.

--- Forwarded message: ---
From: Redwood Marketplace Billing <billing@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Dec 2029 10:05:00 -0800
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Subject: internal: meter-stitch plan

Marcus, Soojin, Jonas — I've started an automated stitch run comparing the Nimbus CSV to our audit manifest and the raw marketplace records we ingest (extracts: aws_metering_logs_202911.zip, gcp_billing_trace_202911.log). Initial pass highlights:
- ~2,800 event IDs in Nimbus CSV that match exactly to our AWS raw events, but are attributed to a different SKU in the AWS payload (likely mapping drift).
- ~1,100 event IDs present in both AWS and GCP extracts but with overlapping timestamps — looks like simultaneous reporting during the platform migration on 2029-11-13.
- ~420 events flagged as retries by AWS (metering_retry_count > 0).

Plan / timeline:
1) Today: run UID-level join and produce three reconciliation buckets (match, mapping-drift, duplicates/retries) — deliverable: reconciliation_summary.csv (internal).
2) Tue 12/03 EOD: present proposed accounting treatment per bucket: credit memo, reclassify SKU, or no action.
3) Wed 12/04: if credit required, draft credit memo and coordinate with Nimbus and AWS/GCP support cases.

Can you confirm Nimbus is OK with joint support cases if we escalate duplicates to the cloud marketplaces? Also confirm whether Nimbus needs the credits applied on Redwood's invoice or Nimbus's merchant payout (they may prefer merchant-side adjustment).

Marcus

--- end forwarded message ---

Ana — for the joint cases, we recommend Redwood opens the initial support cases and cc's Nimbus so we can preserve our inbound ingest logs. If you're comfortable with that, we'll open the AWS/GCP tickets and include the sample payloads you sent. Please confirm merchant-side credit vs Redwood-invoice credit preference.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Ana Cortez <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>, GCP Marketplace Billing <gcp-billing-support@google.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Dec 2029 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stitching AWS/GCP marketplace lines for Nimbus merchant invoice

Marcus / Redwood team — thanks for the summary and the proposed plan. Nimbus confirms:
- They prefer merchant-side adjustments if the marketplaces accept that approach (so credits are issued against Nimbus's merchant payout).
- They want joint support cases so the cloud providers can triage the retry/duplicate signals with both sides' payloads.
- Please open the AWS and GCP support requests and cc our billing alias; include the attached sample_event_ids_11-13.txt and the relevant extracts.

We're available for a 30-minute sync on Wed 12/04 at 10am PT to review the reconciliation buckets and finalize accounting treatment.

Regards,
Ana

---
Ana Cortez
Head of Finance Ops — Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: sample_event_ids_11-13.txt (txt)
